title: Defining, calling and returning from functions
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C language rules.
Trace the example and explain data flow.
Identify common errors and boundary conditions.
Apply the concept in a small tested program.

understand.concept: A function definition specifies a function's return type, name, parameter list and body. A function call evaluates arguments, transfers control to the function and uses the returned value when the function completes with a return expression.
understand.whyItMatters: Functions divide a program into named operations, reduce repetition and make behaviour easier to test independently.
understand.analogy: Treat a function or pointer operation as an explicit contract between caller and callee.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal rules for types, object lifetime, scope and linkage.

explain.narrative:
A function definition specifies a function's return type, name, parameter list and body. A function call evaluates arguments, transfers control to the function and uses the returned value when the function completes with a return expression.

When applying this concept, check declared types, preconditions, object lifetime and all control-flow paths. Compile with warnings enabled and test both typical and boundary inputs.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: maximum receives two int arguments and returns one int. main stores that returned value and prints it. The function's local parameters cease to exist when the call returns.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the argument values, function body and returned result.
practise.independentTask: Write functions for minimum, maximum and absolute difference. Test equal and negative inputs.
hints: A non-void function should return a value compatible with its declared return type on every required path.
A function call expression has a type determined by the function's return type.
Keep each function focused on one clear responsibility.
